title: Agent softphone in the UCC workspace
description: Twilio Voice JS SDK plus TaskRouter JS worker in the React agent workspace, so the agent answers and talks to the caller in the browser with the ticket already on screen.
close_reason: Softphone built: voice-token endpoint (Voice + TaskRouter grants on one Access Token), useSoftphone hook with token refresh and mic pre-flight, Softphone component mounted in the sidebar so a ringing call is visible on every screen. Renders verified in browser.

title: TaskRouter routing and escalation to a queue
description: Map UCC departments to TaskRouter queues and workflows. On escalation, create a task carrying ticket context so the agent gets the AI summary.

title: Stream AI turns to remove the voice pause
description: handleTurn currently does a full Bedrock Converse round trip before returning, roughly 2-3s. On a phone call that is a dead pause after every sentence. Stream tokens so Twilio TTS starts speaking immediately.

title: Inbound AI call via ConversationRelay
description: TwiML webhook plus ConversationRelay websocket handler. Twilio does STT/TTS, our existing handleTurn does reasoning on Bedrock. Creates the UccCall and UccTicket on call start.
close_reason: ConversationRelay inbound path: TwiML answer URL opens the case, websocket runs handleTurn, handoff enqueues to TaskRouter, status callback ends the call. Webhooks are Twilio-signature verified. 7 integration tests.

title: Twilio telephony adapter implementing TelephonyProvider
description: Implement TwilioProvider so UCC can drive real telephony through Twilio instead of Amazon Connect, which is blocked org-wide by SCP p-qocf1ngi. Must satisfy the existing TelephonyProvider port so no application code changes.
close_reason: TwilioProvider implements the TelephonyProvider port; 10 unit tests with a fake SDK client. Factory selects it on UCC_TELEPHONY=twilio and refuses to fall back silently.

title: Supervisor dashboard counted assigned calls as waiting
description: The dashboard 'Waiting in Queue' tile counted every call with status QUEUED. A call keeps QUEUED from queue entry until the agent accepts, so a call already assigned to an agent was counted as waiting. On screen this contradicted the per-queue table (which counts QUEUED_FOR_AGENT tickets and correctly showed 0) and the agent floor (which showed the agent ON CALL). Found by visually verifying the UI, not by the test suite.
design: Split the QUEUED bucket by whether an agent is assigned: waitingCalls (no agent) vs ringingCalls (assigned, not yet accepted). Extracted summariseCallLoad() from the route handler so the distinction is unit-testable.
acceptance_criteria: waitingCalls agrees with the per-queue table; ringing calls are visible; regression tests cover assigned and unassigned cases.
close_reason: Fixed: summariseCallLoad() splits QUEUED into waitingCalls/ringingCalls; both dashboards show the ringing hint; 2 regression tests added (85 passing).
